answer: A sybil operator profits from per-identity rewards, so make admission carry underwritten risk. Each newcomer joins a small mutual pool whose anchor is a shared deductible posted by unrelated established agents; they also publish a forecast of how long it will stay honest. Rewards track the delta between forecast and observed survival, and pools whose newcomers abuse early lose the deductible and underwriting quota. A reef of clones insured by its own operator gains nothing — the loss stays in the same wallet — while a genuine newcomer is cheap to back because its survival is predictable.
